title: Isolated Downstream Validation and Single‑Repair Effects in Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study cand-003-stud-001) that isolates purely downstream deterministic validation plus a bounded single-repair intervention under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using 1,000 deterministic intents (1,000 paired episodes) drawn from a synthetic workflow stress corpus and a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; any paired outcome difference can therefore arise only from the validator decision and at most one permitted repair call (guarded arm). Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; discordants n10 = 5 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only); preregistered primary test exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). Preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.001, 0.01]. Total hosted model calls recorded = 1005 (1000 shared initial + 5 repair). We present the exact McNemar as the confirmatory inference, the bootstrap interval as a preregistered descriptive summary, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, ceiling effects, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating translation from operator intent to device configuration promises efficiency gains but raises safety risks: incorrect ordering, transient invariant violations, and unauthorized touches of protected fields can convert plausible plans into damaging live changes. Prior empirical work documents frequent LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that reduce correctness in code- and config-like generation and motivates verifier‑augmented architectures that detect and sometimes repair unsafe outputs [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment explicitly designed to isolate the incremental effect of a deterministic validator and a single bounded repair invocation when both experimental arms reuse the exact same initial sampled candidate (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Our central empirical estimand is the paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) computed on complete pairs. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics no first‑pass sampling differences exist between arms; therefore any paired outcome difference can only arise from the deterministic validator decision and the allowed at‑most‑one repair call. This clarifies the causal interpretation compared with designs that mix downstream interventions with independent first‑pass generation or decoding changes.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired confirmatory study (Npairs = 1,000) with deterministic task selection from a challenging synthetic NetOps workflow stress corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and explicit runtime configuration reporting (declared model = gpt‑5‑mini; model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset — null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). (3) Transparent reporting of the preregistered primary inference (exact two‑sided McNemar, p = 0.0625), the preregistered paired bootstrap descriptive summary (95% percentile CI = [0.001, 0.01], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), and an evidence‑grounded interpretation that accounts for sparse discordant counts, near‑unity baseline, and validator scope.
sections.related_work:
Empirical studies and surveys establish that LLMs frequently produce hallucinated or semantically incorrect outputs in structured tasks, and that generation behavior is sensitive to prompt and decoding choices; these findings motivate coupling generation with verification layers [1],[2]. Work on constrained or schema‑aware decoding reduces syntactic and executable errors in structured domains, though much evidence originates outside NetOps and relies on downstream validator fidelity when applied to network workflows [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system work emphasizes verifier‑assisted repair, proof‑carrying traces, and governance—these contributions present prototypes and architectural arguments showing that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and externally enforced protocols rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Where prior papers report generate→validate→repair pipelines, improvement magnitudes depend strongly on benchmark design, validator coverage, and whether first‑pass generation differences are permitted. Some benchmarks report clear offline gains when generation and verification are co‑designed, but heterogeneous validator semantics and offline settings limit generalization to live multi‑device NetOps workflows. Our preregistered paired study complements this literature by holding the initial generation constant and isolating only the deterministic downstream validator plus a single repair call; this isolates the effect pathway from validator/repair rather than conflating it with prompt, decoding, or sampling differences.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study preregistration (study id cand‑003‑stud‑001) was frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation and executed by a registered analysis executor. Core preregistered items used without deviation: task_count = 1,000 complete pairs; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both arms); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary confirmatory test = exact two‑sided McNemar. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI used 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 for descriptive summaries.

Task corpus and deterministic selection rule. Tasks derive from the synthetic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus. The preregistered ordinal selection rule deterministically maps zero‑based ordinal j ∈ [0,999] into a unique task_index (cycle and offset pattern described in preregistration) producing exactly 1,000 unique intents. Each manifest includes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and an annotated difficulty label (representative difficulties observed in artifacts include 'very_hard' and 'extreme').

Adapter, model, and validator. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the declared provider/model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The recorded model configuration shows temperature = null/unset; per preregistered reporting this is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The validator is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and implements a digital‑twin emulation that deterministically checks parsed candidate command sequences against manifest constraints (required command presence/order, protected‑field noninterference, and workflow invariants) and emits a binary safe‑deploy decision with structured validator traces.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and causal interpretation. Under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate the baseline and guarded episodes reuse the same initial sampled candidate per pair. The guarded pipeline deterministically validates that candidate and, if the validator rejects it, may invoke at most one repair call (per adapter bounds). Because the initial candidate is identical across arms, only downstream deterministic validation and permitted repair can produce a paired outcome difference; this design therefore reframes the estimand as: baseline single‑shot/initial validity versus final guarded‑pipeline validity after deterministic validation and permitted repair.

Execution bounds and missingness handling. The preregistered maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no retries). The execution used the 'complete_pair_primary' missingness treatment; no episodes failed (failed episodes = 0) so sensitivity treatments for failures were not invoked. The registered analysis executor computed exact paired tests and the preregistered bootstrap summaries.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 2,000; completed = 2,000; complete_pairs = 1,000; failed episodes = 0. Provider call audit: hosted model call event count = 1,005 consisting of 1,000 shared initial generations and 5 repair invocations (stage counts recorded by the deterministic reconciliation artifact).

Primary paired outcomes (preregistered). The observed paired contingency table is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625; under the preregistered α = 0.05 this H1 is not supported.

Preregistered descriptive summary and sensitivity. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) computed by the registered executor is [0.001, 0.01]; this descriptive interval from the preregistered bootstrap excludes zero in this run despite the confirmatory p‑value being >0.05 because bootstrap percentile behavior with extremely sparse discordant counts can produce nonzero bounds. An exploratory one‑sided McNemar (not preregistered) yields p = 0.03125 and is reported explicitly as post‑hoc/exploratory.

Repair mechanics and representative diagnostics. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred. Archived validator traces for repaired cases show concrete repair mechanics: the guarded pipeline rejected the shared initial candidate for violations such as required_sequence ordering errors or touches of protected interfaces, invoked a single repair call that produced a repaired candidate, and revalidated the repaired candidate as acceptable. Representative task manifests and response traces (e.g., required_sequence patterns and difficulty annotations in execution artifacts) illustrate common workflow motifs (failover_then_offline_reconfiguration, rolling_access_vlan_migration, composed_redundancy_and_access_maintenance) that appear in repaired and unrepaired episodes. Total hosted model calls = 1,005 (1,000 shared initial + 5 repair).

Contamination, exclusions, and deterministic reconciliations. Contamination checks recorded no prompt‑leakage flags; no post‑hoc exclusions were applied. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm pair and episode accounting consistency and record that all deterministic consistency checks passed.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive evidence and interpretation. The preregistered primary inference is the exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625); by the preregistered decision rule this does not meet two‑sided α = 0.05 and therefore we do not claim confirmatory support for H1. The preregistered bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a descriptive summary produced by the registered executor; because it was prespecified and computed deterministically it is reported as descriptive only and does not supersede the preregistered confirmatory outcome. The exploratory one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) is explicitly post‑hoc.

Sparse discordant counts, ceiling effects, and power. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline≈0.60 and an absolute target increase of 0.15; observed baseline = 0.995 is far higher than assumed. This concentrates mass in the concordant cell (n11 = 995) and leaves very few discordant pairs (n10 + n01 = 5). Exact paired tests such as McNemar are discrete and sensitive to small discordant counts; with n10 = 5 and n01 = 0 the two‑sided exact p = 0.0625 sits just above the conventional 0.05 threshold. Practically, when baseline validity is near unity, detecting very small absolute gains (here 0.005) requires either far larger pair counts or design changes that increase discordance (for example, independent generation arms, targeted failure injections, or larger permitted repair budgets).

Failure‑mode and difficulty‑pattern diagnostics. The archived validator traces show that the five repaired cases arose from concrete, rule‑level violations the validator was designed to catch (ordering errors in required_sequence and protected‑field touches). Representative task manifests and response traces in the artifact set indicate that repaired episodes disproportionately involve complex multi‑step sequences and composed-redundancy patterns (cataloged with difficulty labels 'very_hard' or 'extreme'), consistent with intuition that multi-step dependency constraints create ordering vulnerabilities. However, only five repairs were observed, so inference about repair efficacy across the full failure modality spectrum is limited: possibilities consistent with the evidence include a low prevalence of validator‑detectable violations in the sampled corpus, generator behavior for the declared model+prompt producing largely valid initial candidates, and validator coverage that may not capture some semantic error classes.

Design rationale and causal clarity. The shared_initial_candidate paired design intentionally isolates downstream validator and repair effects and avoids conflation with prompt/decoding or sampling interventions. This yields a clean causal estimand (baseline single‑shot initial validity versus final guarded validity after deterministic validation and up to one repair) but precludes measuring effects that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompt engineering. For research agendas concerned with overall operational pipelines, both estimands (isolated downstream effect vs. end‑to‑end generator+validator effect) are valuable; our study answers the former precisely and leaves the latter to preregistered follow‑ups.

Operational implications and recommended follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows that verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. Preregistered follow‑ups that align with remaining open questions include: (1) executing independent first‑pass generation arms to measure prompt/decoding intervention effects (not executed here under shared_initial_candidate); (2) sweeping repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns; (3) expanding validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) evaluating multiple model families. Each follow‑up should prespecify realistic baseline failure ranges and adjust power calculations to the expected operating regime.

Threats to validity. Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream effects but prevent measuring first‑pass generation interventions. External validity: the synthetic corpus and single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments. Conclusion validity: extreme baseline success yielded sparse discordant counts and discrete p‑value behavior, reducing sensitivity for small absolute effects. These limitations are cataloged in the preregistration and in the submitted limitations section.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar did not meet two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total hosted model calls recorded = 1,005. The preregistered confirmatory result is the exact McNemar outcome; the paired bootstrap CI and one‑sided test are reported as descriptive and exploratory respectively. Artifact‑grounded evidence indicates downstream validator/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in structured NetOps workflows, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budgets, validator coverage, and model families are necessary to map marginal returns in realistic operating regimes.

disclosure_statement: Declared model and provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the validator/digital twin. Preregistration: study cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls and recorded in the archived execution manifest). Immutable initial master prompt reference archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset (null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Human role and autonomy boundary: after the autonomy lock the research run executed the preregistered experiment, analysis, and manuscript drafting; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
